definitions.explanation: A large earthen mound built as a tomb for rulers and powerful figures in ancient Japan, dating mainly from the 3rd to 7th centuries. The most distinctive type is the keyhole-shaped mound ({前方後円墳|ぜんぽうこうえんふん}).

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{古墳|こふん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{五世紀|ごせいき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ものだ。
examples.english: This burial mound dates from the 5th century.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{世界最大|せかいさいだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{古墳|こふん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Osaka has the world's largest burial mound.

examples.japanese: {古墳|こふん}⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{豪族|ごうぞく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{巨大|きょだい}→巨大：02586_kyodai⟧な⟦{墓|はか}→墓：03549_haka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{築|きず}いた→築く：02046_kizuku⟧。
examples.english: During the Kofun period, many powerful clans built enormous tombs.

notes:
The {古墳|こふん}⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧ (Kofun period, c. 250-538 CE) is named after these burial mounds. The most famous is {仁徳天皇陵|にんとくてんのうりょう} in {堺|さかい}, ⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧, the largest keyhole-shaped tomb in the world. Many {古墳|こふん} have been designated as UNESCO World Heritage sites.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古墳|こふん}⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧ — the Kofun period
- {前方後円墳|ぜんぽうこうえんふん} — keyhole-shaped burial mound
- {古墳|こふん}{群|ぐん} — a group of burial mounds
- {古墳|こふん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発掘|はっくつ}する→発掘する：27001_hakkutsusuru⟧ — to excavate a burial mound
